clue.text: William stocks river fish

indicators.note: a container stocks or holds goods, so the name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Bill is the familiar short form of William

explanation.surface: Somebody called William keeps a supply of fish from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot.

clue.text: Listed work required in a vehicle for the winter

indicators.note: the work is needed inside the vehicle, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a sled is a vehicle that runs over snow
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A catalogued piece of work has to be done inside a winter sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed' here means leaning over, as a ship lists, not catalogued.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has listed is tilted to one side, so its deck is at a slant.

clue.text: Hottest Canadian water the hand can accept

indicators.note: a container can take something in, so the hand goes round the lake

parts.note: a fist is a hand clenched
Lake Erie lies on the border of Canada and the US

explanation.surface: A hand plunged into a Canadian lake finds it as hot as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can accept' signals the container: the hand closes round the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiery things blaze with heat, so the most fiery are the hottest.

clue.text: Cut the favourite bit

parts.note: to snip is to cut with scissors
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A hairdresser trims the part of the hair they like best.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment of something.

clue.text: Hurt about a sailor's pushing off

indicators.note: one piece wraps around the other, here the pain around the seaman

parts.note: a sting is a sharp hurt
TAR is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor feels a pain as he sets off on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor goes in after the first letter of the hurt, splitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing off is setting out, and starting is beginning a journey.

clue.text: Sit eating scrambled egg on something

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sits down to eat scrambled egg on toast or similar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' rearranges SITEATING into the answer. 'egg on' looks like breakfast but is the verb to urge.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate a thing is to urge or provoke it into happening.

clue.text: Outstanding British citizen about all in maybe

indicators.note: the citizen wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a Brit is a British person

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A remarkable Briton is described as having everything included, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' shuffles ALL IN into LLIAN; the citizen wraps round it before his final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant means exceptionally good or dazzling, standing out from the rest.

clue.text: The way a person acquires a jewel

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
one means a person, as in one should

explanation.surface: Someone on the street comes by a precious gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone is a gem set in jewellery.

clue.text: Pole beats retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: raps are knocks or beats

explanation.surface: A Pole defeats an enemy that is falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns RAPS around. 'Pole' looks like a nationality but is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, such as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: Show enthusiasm for gin? Nonsense!

parts.note: to clap is to applaud something
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: Applauding a drink of gin is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' here is the hunter's snare, not the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk designed to win applause.

clue.text: A bad character in the main

definitions.text: A bad character in the main

parts.words: A bad character in the main
parts.note: the main is the open sea, and a villain at sea is a sea robber

explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber who attacks ships on the high seas.

clue.text: Keenness among competitively-minded gentry

indicators.note: the answer is found amid the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Ambition is common among the competitive upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is sharpness or keenness, as in an edge to the voice.

clue.text: Becoming hangers-on

parts.note: becoming means attractive, and these ornaments literally hang from the ears

explanation.definitionFit: These jewels dangle from the lobes and are worn because they flatter the wearer.

clue.text: The lawyer's right — one's involved in trading

indicators.note: these letters are wrapped up within the dealing

parts.note: to barter is to trade goods
one is I, so one's (one is) gives IS

explanation.surface: An attorney insists he is in the right while engaged in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer who argues cases in the higher courts in Britain.

clue.text: Endlessly radio back estimated time of arrival for broadcast

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter
back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone keeps radioing to report the expected arrival time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts RADIO to RADI and 'back' turns ETA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to send out or emit in all directions, as a signal is spread.

clue.text: Being within the fold is swell!

parts.note: within means in
a crease is a fold line

explanation.surface: A sheep welcomed back into the flock is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like a sheep pen and 'swell' like the exclamation of delight; one is a crease, the other a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow larger, which is what an increase does.

clue.text: The craft of the lot without equipment!

indicators.note: here in its old sense of outside, so the lot surrounds the gear

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: A vessel is stripped of all its fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship, a sea-going craft.

clue.text: Retiring woman remains and makes up afresh

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: her refers to a woman
ashes are what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A woman going into retirement leaves relics and starts over.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehash is to rework old material into a new form.

clue.text: Tirades unreasonably mounted

indicators.note: unreasonable implies not in proper order, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Irrational rants have been delivered on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting astride is having a leg on each side, as a rider mounted on a horse.

clue.text: Bangers for a festive occasion

parts.note: bangers suggests sausages, but these are the paper tubes that snap at Christmas dinner

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'bangers' is slang for sausages; here they are things that go bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas crackers are paper tubes pulled apart with a bang at the festive table.

clue.text: A man's circulation

definitions.meaning: a whirl of water or air moving in a circle

explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, and a swirling current that moves round in a loop.

clue.text: Cover made of leather

definitions.meaning: to conceal or screen from sight

explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something, and the skin of an animal tanned for use.

clue.text: Give time to hold on

indicators.note: the time holds the other word inside it

parts.note: a date is a specified time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spare a moment to hang on.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give money or goods to a cause.

clue.text: Some over-sentimental lines written

indicators.note: some means part of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Mawkish poetry has been composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is writing set out in metrical lines, as poetry.

clue.text: Doesn't perhaps supply port abroad

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be ordered differently

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to provide a foreign harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a ferry port on the Belgian coast.

clue.text: Dispatched into the long grass, which is much objected to

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: A ball whacked into the rough is greatly resented by the golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long grass' suggests a lost ball, but it is the waterside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Resented means taken offence at, strongly disliked.

clue.text: The minimum would be fifty — a quarter

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
east is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: The lowest bid would be fifty, a quarter of the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' looks like a fraction but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the smallest amount possible.

clue.text: Publicly declare dive rates demolition

indicators.note: demolishing knocks something apart, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A notice announces that diving charges will be scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To advertise is to make something known to the public.
